alex: Quick heads-up — planning a base-image rebuild tonight 23:00 PST. Couple of tricky bits: keystore rotation + signer role changes + rolling nodes. Want to surface the failure modes now so we don't wake oncall at 2am.

maria: Thanks. What's the desired keystore rotation order? rotate KMS key -> re-encrypt images -> rotate signer SA creds?

alex: Thinking: 1) create new KMS key version (do not disable old) 2) push new cosign key wrapped by new KMS 3) update image signer to use new key, 4) rotate binder roles, 5) disable old key after 24h. Concern: runtime agents pulling images might still try to verify with old key if signatures pinned.

ben: fwiw, the signer service account needs iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob and roles/kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key ring. If we change SA perms in the same window as the key switch, some batch jobs will fail to pull. Suggest a short canary window where both keys/roles valid.

julia: Also audit logging note: when we rewrap signatures we need to ensure audit logs show both cosign:keyID entries. Otherwise the compliance team will flag missing provenance. We should forward GKE audit logs to secure-gcs/archive/kms-rotations.

samir: Also saw a related vuln triage — libc CVE-2026-1234 popped up in the new base. If we rebuild to pick up the libc fix, timing matters: package removal can change layer hash -> breaks artifact provenance checks unless we re-sign everything.

alex: Good call. Proposal: build new base with patched libs, produce image candidate, run cosign verify/attest locally, push to staging registry, run runtime canary for 2 hours, then promote. During canary, keep old signer key accepted by runtime verification policy.

ben: How do we keep runtimes accepting both keys? Can we update the verification artifact to include two key fingerprints? Example policy fragment: 
```
verification: {
  trusted_signatures: ["cosign:sha256:OLD", "cosign:sha256:NEW"]
}
```

maria: ^ that works if runtime verification reads from config map. But note: Redwood runtime has prefix caching for attestation results — we must flush cache on rollout. Otherwise some nodes will still reject. Add cache invalidation step: `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/runtime-proxy` after updating configmap.

julia: On audit side — add a temporary filter so SIEM treats both keys as acceptable for 48h to avoid alerts. I can open ticket with security-monitoring.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: alex triggered image-build pipeline for base-rebuild-candidate-179876. CI job 4721 started.

alex: Thanks. One more edge-case — private Dedicated clusters using offline signing (HSM-backed) won't accept cosign+KMS mix unless we pre-provision wrapped keys. @ben can you confirm we have key-wrapping artifacts for on-prem HSM clusters?

ben: I will check. If not, fallback is: keep old signed images available in the on-prem registry and run a staggered cutover. Don't rotate HSM keys on the same night as base rebuild.

samir: Also adding quick incident plan: if runtime fails verification en masse, revert by: 1) re-enable old key in KMS, 2) update verification config to only trust OLD, 3) restart runtime proxy, 4) roll back image promotion. Document will live in confluence: /security/base-image-rotations/playbook.

maria: Action items: @ben verify HSM wrapped-key availability for on-prem by 17:00 PT; @julia open SIEM suppression ticket; @alex schedule canary for 23:00 and coordinate oncall.

alex: Sounds good. I'll post a short runbook snippet in the thread once I finalize timings. :thumbsup:

ben: Quick command I used to check cosign fingerprints: 
```
cosign verify --key kms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/base-signing old-image:sha256
```

julia: And SIEM rule to mute (example): `event.attributes.signature.key_id IN (OLD,NEW) AND event.timestamp BETWEEN t0 AND t0+48h`

alex: OK closing loop — will update by 20:30 PT. Thanks all.
